topic.title: Print culture and the modern world
topic.scope: printing in China, Gutenberg, print and reformation, print in India, debates, censorship

concepts.name: Origins and Evolution of Printing Technology

misconceptions.statement: Johannes Gutenberg invented the very first printing press in the world.
misconceptions.why: Textbooks often highlight Gutenberg's press as the starting point of the modern era, ignoring earlier Asian developments.
misconceptions.fix: Woodblock printing existed in China, Japan, and Korea centuries before Gutenberg developed his mechanical metal-type press in Europe.

probe.question: Where did the earliest form of printing technology originate?
probe.wrong_answer: It started in Germany with Gutenberg's invention.

misconceptions.statement: The Catholic Church was the primary force that encouraged the spread of printed books to educate the masses.
misconceptions.why: Students often conflate the Church's role in preserving manuscripts with the later reaction to mass-produced books.
misconceptions.fix: The Church initially viewed mass-printed books as a threat to its authority and established the Index of Prohibited Books to censor them.

probe.question: How did the Catholic Church react to the spread of printed religious texts?
probe.wrong_answer: They supported it because it helped spread Christianity to more people.

misconceptions.statement: Printing in India was introduced solely by the British government to spread literacy among Indians.
misconceptions.why: Students assume that all colonial infrastructure was designed for the benefit of the local population.
misconceptions.fix: Printing was first brought to India by Portuguese missionaries for religious purposes, and later used by Indians for social reform and political debate.

probe.question: What was the primary motive for introducing printing in India?
probe.wrong_answer: The British government wanted to educate the Indian public.

misconceptions.statement: All printed newspapers in colonial India were controlled by the British government.
misconceptions.why: Students often view colonial rule as a monolithic power that controlled every aspect of public life.

probe.question: Could Indian nationalists use newspapers to criticize the British?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because the British owned and censored all printing presses in India.

misconceptions.fix: While the British imposed censorship like the Vernacular Press Act, many Indian-owned newspapers actively used print to challenge colonial policies.
